newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain unions want work halted in anti-ETA protest.
newsitem.headline: Spain unions want work halted in anti-ETA protest.

text.p: Trade unions called on workers throughout Spain to stop work and observe 10 minutes of silence on Monday in protest against the kidnap-murder of a politician by Basque separatist guerrillas.
Basque political leaders urged a one-hour stoppage in the Basque region only at noon on Monday.

In a joint statement, the country's two leading trade unions -- the General Workers' Union (UGT) and the Workers' Commissions Union (CCOO) -- expressed "profound sadness and indignation" at the killing of 29-year-old Miguel Angel Blanco, a Basque town councillor.
They asked workers to stop and observe 10 minutes of silence at noon on Monday.

The Basque separatist group ETA kidnapped Blanco on Thursday and killed him on Saturday after the Spanish government rejected its demand for a transfer of some 500 inmates scattered around the country to Basque prisons.
The kidnap-murder triggered mass protest demonstrations around Spain on Friday and Saturday attended by more than a million people.
On Sunday, violence erupted between ETA supporters and opponents in Pamplona near the Basque region.
